newsitem.title: USA: Reno reviews Clinton, Dole campaign finance request.
newsitem.headline: Reno reviews Clinton, Dole campaign finance request.

text.p: Attorney General Janet Reno said on Thursday she is reviewing a request for an independent counsel to investigate alleged violations of finance laws by the Democratic and Republican presidential campaigns.

"At this point, I don't know what is appropriate because I don't know what I'm going to find," Reno said of the letter from the citizens' lobbying group Common Cause demanding she seek the appointment of an independent counsel.

Common Cause alleged that President Bill Clinton's primary committee, working through the Democratic National Committee, and Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole's primary committee, working through the Republican National Committee, illegally schemed to circumvent federal campaign finance laws.
Both the White House and Dole's campaign denied any violations.

"What I'm doing right now is reviewing the letter and the independent counsel statute, with the issues raised in the letter. I can't at this point say what I will do because I don't know what conclusions I (will) reach," Reno said.
She said at her weekly Justice Department news conference the letter just had been received on Wednesday.
Asked if the request would be seriously evaluated, Reno said, "I always try to treat everything the way it should be treated." Reno vowed to make an "appropriate determination."
Reno said the Justice Department would review if there had been an accusation of a real criminal act.
Common Cause called for an independent counsel because Reno's Justice Department would have a "political conflict of interest" in pursuing the case. Clinton appointed Reno.
The group did not bring its complaint to the Federal Election Commission, which oversees campaign spending, because of what it charged as past failures by the federal agency to enforce the law.
